findings.title: ETF and settlement language was too broad
findings.evidence: Category-specific ETF rules cannot support an all-ETF T+0/T+1 claim; exchange language supports settlement-before-sale with specified reverse-trading exceptions rather than a universal shorthand.
findings.repair: Changed the report to settlement-before-sale wording, required product-specific checks and stated that category-specific ETF mechanics cannot be generalised.
findings.verification: Final reader text explicitly contains the category-specific and settlement caveats.

findings.title: Price-limit discussion could be read as a universal percentage rule
findings.evidence: Board, fund category, special status and listing stage vary.
findings.repair: Added explicit heterogeneous price-limit wording and the warning that no price limit does not imply exit liquidity.
findings.verification: China-constraint chapter and case verifier contain the exact boundary.

findings.title: Chinese reader-facing text used critical foreign investment abbreviations without first-use definitions
findings.evidence: LBO, KPI, IRR, PE, TAM, ALM and alpha appeared in decision, valuation, risk and catalyst logic without Chinese first-use explanations.
findings.repair: Added first-use Chinese definitions for leverage buyout, key performance indicator, internal rate of return, price-to-earnings, total addressable market, asset-liability management and alpha; retained abbreviations only after definition.
findings.verification: Reader-text and case-verifier checks confirm the required definitions are present.

findings.title: Unverified ranking language could imply a proven manager or strategy hierarchy
findings.evidence: Terms such as top, strongest, best and optimal appeared without a ranking methodology or performance comparison.
findings.repair: Recast the language to the report's reference managers and its own framework, retaining the no-alpha/no-performance-proof boundary.
findings.verification: Current reader-facing chapters avoid a ranking conclusion.
